cohort: 120 pregnant women (60 with multiple pregnancies and 60 with singleton pregnancies) delivering at a tertiary care center in Purnea, Bihar.
finding: Multiple pregnancies are associated with a higher incidence of maternal and neonatal complications, including preterm delivery, anemia, hypertensive disorders, cesarean section, low birth weight, NICU admission, and neonatal mortality, compared to singleton pregnancies.
mod_finding: The incidence of cesarean section was significantly higher in the multiple pregnancy group.
